reviews.author: Sharon W.
reviews.text: The site map did not list my space as handicap. While it would have been excellent if you're in a wheelchair, for me it was horrible. I felt like I was camped in a fishbowl. The path to the bathroom directly led to my tent site, so everyone's flashlight shone directly into my tent. That combined with the sound of flushing toilet's led to a sleepless night. I left after one night.

reviews.author: Kevin L.
reviews.text: Great campsites and good checkin.  We'll be back.

reviews.author: Maria H.
reviews.text: Loved this campground, wish we could have stayed longer! There are a couple of trails directly from the campground that were amazing, so many different fungi and mosses. Close to the beautiful beach as well.

reviews.author: Ashley G.
reviews.text: Very close to Rialto Beach.  Facilities were clean and campsite was spacious in D loop.

reviews.author: Christopher G.
reviews.text: First trip to the Olympic Peninsula was absolutely amazing. This campground was extremely clean and quiet, also very close to Rialto beach. My family can't wait to come back next year!

reviews.author: Andrew R.
reviews.text: Our site was large, clean, and distant from other sites. Well maintained, and the facilities were well taken care of. Only a couple of miles from Rialto Beach; can’t complain. Can’t wait to come back here!

reviews.author: Allison D.
reviews.text: Right fit for a 4 man tent and the table and fire pit. Glad it was so wet because if it were dryer I don’t know if we could have had a fire with how close it was to the fire pit. Not a complain because it was a great spot that had privacy and shade. Loves this campground to pieces.

reviews.author: So Heui K.
reviews.text: Saw a housekeeping staff clean his mop at drinking water site.  Grossed me out.

reviews.author: Xiaohong  L.
reviews.text: Nice and clean,very quiet place definitely come back

reviews.author: Samuel S.
reviews.text: Good site.  Plenty of space for a 23’ RV or larger, and an additional vehicle.

reviews.author: Samuel S.
reviews.text: Nice location. Originally had reservations at C-46 which the claimed would take a 22’ RV. It would not, but this site A-10, which claimed to only take a 17’ foot RV actually accommodated a 23’ RV.

reviews.author: irene h.
reviews.text: Quiet campground in a beautiful setting. Plenty of privacy. Restrooms were clean.

reviews.author: Lydia B.
reviews.text: We had an amazing time at Mora! Good distance between each site, the bathrooms are relatively clean, and the forest is magical. Wish it was a little closer to Rialto beach. We got rained on the second night pretty bad which is to be expected in the rainforest - make sure you have a rain fly and tarps/canopies!

reviews.author: Steven H.
reviews.text: Stayed in B22 & B23, they are very close to each other like the description says, but private from other neighboring sites.  Both sites are big, both can hold at least 2 tents.  Campground had clean bathrooms, though the men's room had no soap.  Water was easy to access/fill.  They weren't selling firewood when we were there, but there is plenty on the way in.

reviews.author: Jason C.
reviews.text: Clean facilities and private sites. Rialto Beach is a must see!

reviews.author: Linda-Ann R.
reviews.text: Though a large campground it was quiet, people were considerate and respectful. Bathroom clean but no soap. Due to COVID no showers. Getting water was always a walk, only by the restrooms. Loved the location, easy drives to beaches, lakes and places to  play.

reviews.author: hazel b.
reviews.text: Awesome place! So close to Rialto Beach

reviews.author: Casey J.
reviews.text: Wonderful campground, very clean, quiet, and close to waterfront and gas and snacks. Affordable, and fun!

reviews.author: Ulrike K.
reviews.text: Great quiet site and easy access to other areas of the park (Ozette, Ho). A resort store nearby is very convenient.

reviews.author: Sarah J.
reviews.text: Lovely campground in the trees with plenty of space.  Definitely in the rainforest as everything was damp each morning but what else would you expect. Easy drive down to the beach.

reviews.author: Michael H.
reviews.text: In many ways a beautiful campground but also deceptively restrictive.  It is located right on a beautiful river, except there is no access to the river.   It is a mile from the beach, but if you have a motorhome or RV, you are not allowed down the road to the beach as their is no large vehicle parking.  The staff have very limited and restricted hours.   A quiet and clean campground but a very restrictive and limited vibe.

reviews.author: Amanda W.
reviews.text: We love this campground.  Reservation only really changes it in a negative at, however.

reviews.author: Amanda S.
reviews.text: Campsites were cool, shady, and spacious. Plenty of space for parking and enough space for multiple tents in our site (58D), though the rocky ground was hard to stake in. Bathrooms were older but clean. There were several families with kids who were screaming and playing until 9 or 10pm but quiet during sleeping hours. Rialto Beach is 2 miles away, jam packed on a summer weekend.

reviews.author: OCTAVIA G.
reviews.text: Great place beautiful scenery

reviews.author: Michael V.
reviews.text:
This is a great campground. The campsites are very spacious. There are no hookups at any site but this is a National Park, not your local KOA. They have pull-throughs for large campers as well.  Make sure to make reservations well in advance. This campground fills up fast!

For nearby activities, there is Realto Beach. I would actually recommend against that beach. There are way too many people there and the beach is only adequate. I much prefer the beaches further south. It might seem like a long drive but 30 minutes away are much better beaches. If you are visiting from out of town, 30 minutes is not very far.

reviews.author: Neal T.
reviews.text: Bring a rain coat and make sure you have a good rain fly for your tent

reviews.author: Ian H.
reviews.text: Always an amazing time. We love coming here. All the sites we’ve camped in have been quiet and private. And the beach just down the road is simply breathtaking.

reviews.author: tevis h.
reviews.text: The Camp host here were SO LOVELY and helpful! beautiful spot.

reviews.author: Jenna S.
reviews.text: Nice campground and bathrooms were really clean. Main complaint is there isn’t a walking trail from the campground to the beach. It’s less than a mile away but there’s nowhere to walk, except on the road. The least they could have is a trail alongside the road.

reviews.author: Rajith G.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground and recently upgraded facilities.

reviews.author: Krista M.
reviews.text: Campsite 2A is amazing! Highly recommend camping here great spot. Right next to Rialto Beach 4mile round trip walking distance, close to the river spotted some bald eagles and wild otters! A short drive away is a nice mini-mart with snacks, booze and firewood! Easy camping experience and gorgeous!

reviews.author: Krista M.
reviews.text: Incredible campground!

reviews.author: John D.
reviews.text: Easy camping...near Rialto Beach and La Push...great camp sites...and James Pond is cool...

reviews.author: Terra C.
reviews.text: One of my favorite campgrounds! Lots of good sites. Spent our weekend back and forth between the campground and Rialto Beach.

reviews.author: Alejandra L.
reviews.text: Beautiful location and campsite. Very serene and not too crowded.

reviews.author: Dennison L.
reviews.text: A bit out of the way if you intend to visit Hurricane, Sol Duc, and Hoh Rainforest regions, but perfect for the beaches. While most people would prefer to get a wilderness pass and camp on the beach, most of that is shut down during COVID and Mora campground is the best campground for quick and easy access to the beach. Facilities were very clean, although I wish there were a shower. At least I didn't find one...

reviews.author: Shivani K.
reviews.text: Beautiful woody campground and clean bathroom facilities. Next to the ranger station. Very near to Rialto beach.

reviews.author: Emily W.
reviews.text: Expansive campground. Beautiful area. Dickey River is nearby and looks amazing for kayaking.  We didn't know it was there, so next time, definitely bringing a kayak. No parking there, so you'll have to drop off your gear. Nice bathrooms in campground. If you're looking for hiking trails near the campground, there aren't any, but short .01 walk to James Pond. Drive to or walk along the highway to Rialto Beach. Some campsites are smaller than others, so check the various site loops A, D, E, etc. Loop A are smaller sites and those in loop D or E are bigger, more space for tents, motor home, vehicles, etc.

reviews.author: Gladys G.
reviews.text: Wish we had more nights to stay. 1min walk to the bathroom. There’s a short cut through the loop. Space was smaller than pictures shown. We had 5 of us and 3 tents fit nicely. 2 vehicles fit perfectly. Quiet, love the nature. Bathrooms don’t have any soaps or toilet cover protectors. Water faucets available outside of bathroom to fill up any water jugs.
